plugins_comment: pnpm installs into a symlinked store, and Stryker's default plugin discovery globs `node_modules/@stryker-mutator/*` without following those links: it finds nothing and fails with `Cannot find TestRunner plugin "karma"`. Naming the plugin is not belt-and-braces, it is the only thing that loads it here.
karma_comment: Overrides applied on top of karma.conf.js. `codeCoverage=false` below turns the istanbul instrumentation off; this also drops the `coverage` reporter, whose `check.global` thresholds in karma.conf.js are written for the whole suite and would fail every mutant run, which executes a handful of specs.
timeoutMS_comment: Stryker's allowance is netTime * timeoutFactor + timeoutMS, and `netTime` is time spent *in* the tests: 5.9s here, against 15.4s of karma round-trip overhead the allowance would otherwise ignore. The default 5000 gives ~14s for a run that really costs ~21s, so every mutant needing a full-suite run timed out — and a Timeout counts as *detected*, so those mutants were scored as killed without any assertion having objected. 30s covers the overhead. `assert-mutation-score.mjs` fails on any Timeout for the same reason.
concurrency_comment: MUST stay 1. See docs/mutation-testing.md: with more than one test-runner process the run reports false survivors non-deterministically — measured on 4 runs of one 24-mutant file, concurrency 2 returned 24/24 killed twice and 13/11 and 12/12 the other two times, while concurrency 1 returned 24/24 on all four. `assert-mutation-score.mjs` fails if this is raised, because the symptom is a score that drops for no reason in the source.
maxTestRunnerReuse_comment: 15 is the only value measured to give the same answer on two different machines, and it is not a free parameter in either direction. Unset (Stryker's default, infinite reuse) the karma worker degrades: a 29-mutant local run returned Killed for mutants 0-18 and Timeout for 19-28, clustered by position in the run rather than by mutant, worker at 5.5GB - and a Timeout counts as detected, so the score still read 100% with ten mutants unmeasured. Restarting *more* often is worse, not safer: at 5, CI scored idle-countdown.ts at 20.83% and the local run had survivors and timeouts by its thirteenth mutant. At 15, idle-countdown.ts measured 100% on 24 mutants on both a 4-core/16GB box and a 2-core GitHub runner. Why both directions hurt is not understood; see docs/mutation-testing.md.
ignorePatterns_comment: Sandbox contents only — this does not narrow what is mutated, and `assert-mutation-score.mjs` pins the one entry that does exclude a test. Everything but that entry is weight: the copy drops from 1213 files to 338.
coverageAnalysis_comment: `perTest` runs only the specs covering a mutant. `off` and `all` run the whole suite per mutant and are the fallback if a result is ever in doubt - they are what the early false survivors were confirmed against by hand - at several times the cost.
